thread.title: Apple Earnings: Catalyst To $1 Trillion Market Cap?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Earnings: Catalyst To $1 Trillion Market Cap?
text:
If Apple ( AAPL ) delivers an upbeat June-quarter earnings report next week, it could lift the company to a $1 trillion market cap.
X That's a milestone no company has yet reached, but others like Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) are still in the hunt.
Apple stock is trading just below its all-time high of 195.96, reached on Thursday. Its shares slipped 1.7% to 190.98 on the stock market today . Apple stock had a market valuation of about $939 billion at the end of the regular session Friday.
E-commerce and cloud computing giant Amazon.com has a market capitalization of about $882 billion. Software leader Microsoft has a market cap of $827 billion.

Analysts expect the Cupertino, Calif.-based company to earn $2.18 a share on sales of $52.34 billion. That would translate to year-over-year growth of 31% in earnings per share and 15% in sales.
Gorilla Trades strategist Ken Berman believes Apple earnings will help it breach $1 trillion in market value.
"I predict an all-around beat, the fifth consecutive one," he said in a report Thursday. Berman expects Apple to report a heavier mix of higher-end iPhones sold as well as continued momentum in iPads and services.
Apple Pushing Pricier iPhones Apple's ability to get consumers to spend more on new iPhones is critical to its success, Daniel Morgan, senior portfolio manager of Synovus Trust, said in a report Friday.
In the March quarter, iPhone unit sales rose just 2.5% year over year, but average selling prices increased 11% to $728 a phone. That pushed iPhone revenue up 14% for the period.
For the current quarter, Morgan sees iPhone revenue rising 15% despite flat unit sales, thanks to a 15% boost in average selling prices.
For the September quarter, he forecasts iPhone revenue climbing 20% on flat unit sales, but a 19% lift in average selling prices.
Gearing Up For New iPhones The third quarter is usually a quiet one for Apple as the company prepares to launch its fall lineup of new smartphones and other devices. Apple is widely expected to introduce three new iPhone models in September: two with OLED displays and one with a traditional LCD screen.
For the September quarter, Wall Street is modeling Apple to earn $2.65 a share on sales of $59.57 billion. That would translate to growth of 28% in earnings per share and 13% in sales.
Key metrics for the June-quarter report will be iPhone unit sales and average selling prices as well as services revenue.
Wall Street expects Apple to sell 41.8 million iPhones in the June quarter, vs. 41 million in the year-earlier period.
'Next Big Catalyst' Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty expects Apple to post an in-line June quarter and guide slightly below consensus views for the September quarter.
The launch of new iPhones in September will be the "next big stock catalyst," she said in a report Monday. She raised her price target on Apple stock to 232 from 214 and maintained her overweight rating.
Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi said investor focus has already shifted to Apple's 12th-generation iPhones and expected demand for those handsets in fiscal 2019, which starts Sept. 30.
Wall Street will be looking for clues about the new phones from the Apple report, he said in a note Monday. He rates Apple stock as market perform with a price target of 190.
